settings.heading: By hour ten it is not the rain.
settings.lede: A good boot already keeps water out. What it also does, across a twelve-hour shift, is keep everything your foot produces on the inside of it.
settings.image_alt: All Day in Boots in HydroSox waterproof socks

settings.heading: The problem changes shape after lunch.
settings.lede: For the first few hours a waterproof boot is doing its job well. The longer it stays on, the more of what it is sealing in comes from the foot rather than from the weather.

settings.title: Sweat has nowhere to go
settings.body: A sealed boot with a soaked lining is wet whether or not it has rained. The dampness at the end of a shift usually is not weather.

settings.title: Wet skin is what blisters
settings.body: Softened skin and a seam in the same place for ten hours is the mechanism. Dry skin takes far more rubbing before it gives.

settings.title: The boots go back on tomorrow
settings.body: Work boots rarely get a full day to dry. Monday's damp lining is still there on Tuesday morning.

settings.heading: Built to move vapour, not only to block water.
settings.head_note: The membrane works in both directions. On a long shift, the outward direction is the one that decides how the day ends.

settings.title: Breathable, not just waterproof
settings.body: Porelle® is a waterproof-breathable laminate. Vapour from the foot moves out through it while liquid water cannot come in.

settings.title: The knit next to the skin
settings.body: The inner layer is a soft knit that moves sweat off the foot and keeps the membrane itself off your skin.

settings.title: PFOA free, and stated
settings.body: The chemistry is published rather than left unmentioned — which is worth something for a layer worn against skin ten hours a day.

settings.heading: The same pair, in the conditions this page is about.
settings.head_note: Product imagery rather than a documentary shoot, so read it for what the sock is and where it goes — not as evidence. The checkable claim is the membrane.

settings.title: Rotate them
settings.body: Two or three pairs across a week means each one dries properly between wears, which is also how you get the most life out of a membrane.

settings.title: Check the boot fit once
settings.body: They sit a little thicker than a cotton work sock. Worth one shift's attention if your boots are already tight over the instep.

settings.title: No conditioner, no tumble dryer
settings.body: Fabric conditioner blocks a membrane and dryer heat degrades one. A cool wash and air-drying is the whole routine.

settings.heading: Stated plainly.
settings.body: Breathable does not mean dry inside. Work hard enough, in a sealed boot, and you will produce sweat faster than any membrane can move it. This slows that down. It does not repeal it.
